parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  A report is more than a collection of paragraphs — it is an argument that FLOWS. Each paragraph should connect smoothly to the next, so the reader is guided through your thinking step by step.
content: 📖 A report is more than a collection of paragraphs — it is an argument that FLOWS. Each paragraph should connect smoothly to the next, so the reader is guided through your thinking step by step.

TRANSITIONS are the bridges between paragraphs. A weak report just jumps from one idea to the next. A strong report uses transitions to show relationships: How does this paragraph add to the previous one? Does it contrast? Does it give an example? Does it move from problem to solution?

There are several types of transitions: Adding transitions ('Furthermore...', 'In addition...', 'Moreover...') show you are expanding on an idea. Contrasting transitions ('However...', 'On the other hand...', 'In contrast...') show a different perspective. Cause-effect transitions ('As a result...', 'Therefore...', 'Consequently...') connect cause and effect. Concluding transitions ('To summarize...', 'Overall...', 'In conclusion...') signal the end.
